chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Hafs al-Awar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When the Muhrim (person in Ihram) catches game, ask him: 'Did you catch game before this while you were in Ihram?' If he says yes, tell him: 'Indeed, Allah is avenging against you, so beware of the retribution.' If he says no, judge him to pay the compensation for that game."

key_terms.اَلْمُحْرِمُ: The pilgrim in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: How to determine if a Muhrim's killing of game was accidental or intentional according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) details the procedural mechanism for distinguishing between accidental and intentional hunting violations during Hajj, a key distinction in Shia jurisprudence for determining the specific type of compensation (damm). The method of questioning serves as a practical test of the pilgrim's state of mind, reflecting the scholarly emphasis on intent (niyyah) in penal rulings. It underscores the balance between divine justice and mercy, as the penalty scales with the degree of culpability.
